newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia to resume talks with London Club - agency.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia to resume talks with London Club - agency.

text.p: Talks with the London Club of creditor banks on re-scheduling Yugoslavia's debts will resume in Belgrade on Wednesday, the Yugoslav government said.

The Yugoslav proposal for the rescheduling of debts is based on the Yugoslav economy's realistic possibilities of fulfilling its obligations towards its creditors, the government said in a statement quoted by Tanjug news agency.

"Additional information requested by commercial banks' representatives about the sources and dynamics of the inflow and outflow of funds to and from the Yugoslav econony as the basis for the rescheduling of obligations will be reviewed at the talks," the government said.
Yugoslavia asked in mid-June for a writeoff of 80 per cent of its outstanding $2.4 billion debt, and restructuring the remaining $481 million through a 25-year syndicated loan facility.
Talks held in London on June 24 ended without result, and analysts said the proposal was likely to be rejected.
